newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends slightly higher.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices were slightly higher midsession Wednesday, as the market continued to consolidate after sharp falls last week.
"There was some physical interest, but not enough to turn this market around," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said.
"The reality is the large buyers who were around this time last year are not there this year, with many actually turning into net exporters," she said.
CSCE March world sugar ended up 0.11 cent at 10.62 cents a pound, after seeing a session high at 10.63 cents, as the market recovered from last week's lows at 10.44 cents.
The March/May contango spread narrowed to 0.06 cent from 0.10 cent Tuesday.

"Unlike last year, there is little concern about deliverable supplies against the March contract, though futures and options open interest is still quite high and will impact before long," Ganes said.

In news Wednesday, the Jamaican goverment said arsonists had burned cane fields that would have yielded 1,500 tonnes of sugar, but Jamaican raw production is projected at 256,000 tonnes, up from 238,000 last year, analysts said.
Supply/demand fundamentals remain slightly bearish also, with world sugar stocks increasing, European production better than expected, and India exports seen up.
-- Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
